optionsExempt.description: the lesson is a single thing by nature and has no alternatives to offer — the guided tour, the placement test, the posture checklist. Exempts it from the three-alternatives rule (docs/00 D21). Orientation only; it is not a way to ship a thin practice rung, and validate.py reports how many lessons use it.

levelBand.description: [min, max] level across this rung's options (replan §1.7). A rung is an order within a track; `level` is global difficulty, and the two are allowed to disagree — a Stage 6 rung can hold a level-7 piece, because the easiest complete Joplin rag is a Grade 6 piece. The lesson page prints the band so the learner is told rather than surprised. Generated by tools/content/ladder_report.py's sibling pass and checked by validate.py: every option's level must fall inside it.

tools.description: The modes this rung's material suits, drawn as controls on the lesson page (docs/04 §3d, added 2026-09-18). Sixty lessons gained a 'Tools for this rung' paragraph in b4fb15b and a paragraph cannot be tapped: chords-pop.3 tells the learner to pick D and take I-IV-V-I in the accompaniment lab, which is now one preset chip the lesson has no way to open. The prose stays — it says why a mode suits this rung, which a button cannot. Only modes that have an address are listed: rhythm-only is a remembered setting the Library writes before navigating, so it cannot be opened by a route and a button for it would be a control that does the wrong thing. 'ladder' was in the same position until 2026-09-22 and is not any more — the tempo ladder is run state scoped to a loop, and on a scale, an arpeggio, a Hanon number or an octave study the whole item IS the loop, so ?ladder=1 sets that loop and turns the ladder on as one action. It is for those rungs only (docs/04 §3d names all seven): a whole-piece loop is absurd on repertoire, and a rung wanting the ladder over a piece would have to name bars, which is a different feature.

preset.description: For kind 'lab': which preset in LAB_PRESETS. validate.py refuses one the lab does not have.

item.description: For the Score-screen modes: which of this rung's own song options to open. Omitted, the button takes the rung's first playable song. validate.py refuses an id the rung does not offer, because a lesson may not point outside its own options. A 'simon' names one of the rung's exercises instead, since it opens a drill. A 'ladder' takes no item at all: it opens the rung's first exercise that is notation, and an item written on one is refused by the song-option rule.

label.description: Overrides the button's default wording where the rung wants something shorter or more specific.

unlock.description: For kind 'lab' with a preset: which of the controls that preset locks this rung hands back. Added 2026-09-22, replacing the shape Entry 24 item 5 gave six rungs — a second lab entry with no preset at all, so the lesson page drew two buttons opening the same screen and the prose had to name both. One button that says what it frees is the same offer with half the controls. validate.py refuses a name the rung's own preset does not lock, because 'this frees the tempo' about a tempo nothing fixed is a sentence with no referent.

mode.description: For kind 'lab': which of the three ways round the lab opens on (docs/04 §3c) — bed only, the bed holding the chords, or the bed playing the tune. Added 2026-09-22 for the rungs Entry 30 named as waiting: jam.5, 3.2 and chords-pop.9 each want the opposite of what their shared preset opens on, and until a rung could say so the preset's own default was the only answer and three lessons described a chip the learner had to find.

requires.description: What at least one of this rung's song options must actually be, checked by validate.py against the catalog's `notation` block — which is read from the MusicXML and never from a title. Added 2026-09-18 after four songs were placed on rungs by name: an eleven-bar right-hand melody with no chord symbols went onto the rung teaching left-hand chords, a piece in F major onto the rung teaching the minor, and a 4/4 carol onto the rung teaching the waltz bass. Each key is checked against at least ONE option rather than all of them, because a rung offers alternatives and needs one that demonstrates the thing. This narrows; it does not judge — a piece in 3/4 is not necessarily a waltz, and the brief in docs/prompts/P22 says so.

chordSymbols.description: true when the rung teaches reading or playing from chord symbols: at least one option must print some (`notation.chordCount` above zero).

meter.description: Time signatures as written, e.g. ["3/4"] or ["6/8", "12/8"]. At least one option must carry one of them.

mode.description: At least one option's key signature must say so. A key with no `<mode>` in the file does not count as either, which is the safe direction.

staves.description: At least one option must have this many staves. Two is how a rung says it needs a piece with a left hand, which is what the twelve-bar fault came down to.

songOptional.description: true when no song tests this unit’s skill (reading by interval, the first scale, accompaniment patterns, the theory and improvisation tracks). The lesson then completes on two exercises, and validate.py checks the three-alternatives rule against the combined option count instead of the songs alone (docs/00 D21, docs/02 Part G).

custom.description: free text for checks the engine implements specially, e.g. 'pedal-clean>=0.9'

finder.description: How the owner is to go and find more music for this rung (replan §4.1). Data, not prose: `tools/content/finder.py` generates the search query and the chat prompt from these fields into the built curriculum, so one wording change fixes every rung at once and validate.py can check the result.

skill.description: what the rung trains, in the words a person would use

levelWords.description: the level in plain words, because 'level 3.2' means nothing to a search engine

constraints.description: what the piece must have. Every one of these must appear in the generated prompt; validate.py checks.

avoid.description: what makes a piece wrong for this rung even at the right level

note.description: `bundled` is already in the catalog and names the sound wanted; `wanted` is a piece no reachable source had (replan §1.5), which is why it is in a finder and not an option.

formats.description: which file formats to ask for, and what the app can do with each

searchQuery.description: GENERATED by tools/content/finder.py into the built curriculum. Never authored: it is written from levelWords and constraints, so editing it by hand would be overwritten on the next build.

chatPrompt.description: GENERATED by tools/content/finder.py into the built curriculum. validate.py checks the length, that every constraint survived into it, and that it carries the docs/00 D18 sentence about copyright.

paperHint.description: What to play from a book instead, if he has one (replan §5.2). Prose rather than data: a method book is not searchable, he is looking at a shelf. Required on the Stage 1-5 core rungs and on every classical rung, where a method book or an album almost certainly has an equivalent; optional elsewhere.

concepts.description: GENERATED into the built curriculum from content/curriculum/concepts.json: the display name for every concept id used anywhere, and a finder for the ones that are musical skills rather than features of this app.
